jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in New York City, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in New York City, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it — City Council district, community board, NYPD precinct and sector, community school district, borough, U.S. House, and New York State Senate and Assembly districts — and who represents you.
jsonld.keywords: NYC City Council district map, what council district am I in, NYPD precinct, community board, community school district, New York State Assembly district, New York State Senate district, congressional district, who represents me NYC

brand.tagline: Click the map for every district you're in, and who represents you.

head.title: What district am I in? — districtry New York City
head.description: Tap the map or search a New York City address: Council district, community board, NYPD precinct, school, state — and who represents you. Free, no login.

credits.label: NYC Open Data

credits.label: U.S. Census Bureau (TIGERweb)
credits.note: Congressional and New York State legislative district geometry, and the county boundaries the judicial districts are relabelled from.

credits.label: OpenStreetMap contributors (Photon/Komoot)
credits.note: The cross-metro lookup that offers a hand-off when a point falls in a sibling city.

credits.label: NYC Planning (GeoSearch)
credits.note: Address search and the office-address pins.

credits.label: NYC Council
credits.note: The Council Member roster joined to the City Council district card.

credits.label: NYPD
credits.note: Precinct commanding officers, where the department publishes one.

credits.label: OpenStates
credits.note: District-office addresses for state legislators, where it publishes them.

credits.label: unitedstates/congress-legislators
credits.note: The U.S. House roster joined to the congressional district card.

credits.label: MySchools

layers.label: Borough / County
rank_comment: borough / judicial-district / BP / DA are the same 5 county polygons —

source.answers: Which borough — and therefore which county — this address is in.

boundary.label: Borough boundaries from NYC Open Data (gthc-hcne), shoreline-clipped, simplified and shipped with the app

source.people: Borough-wide officeholders ship with the app and are surfaced on the Borough President and District Attorney cards rather than here.

source.answers: Which New York Supreme Court judicial district covers this address.

boundary.label: The five boroughs relabelled to their judicial districts (1, 2, 11, 12, 13), from the Census Bureau's TIGERweb State_County service — no live source publishes these directly

source.people: No roster is joined; the card links the court system rather than naming justices from an unverifiable list.

source.answers: Which Borough President's office covers this address.

boundary.label: No boundary of its own: this layer draws the borough geometry above and differs only by the office it names

source.people: Borough Presidents ship with the app from the city's own directory.

source.answers: Which District Attorney's office covers this address.

boundary.label: No boundary of its own: this layer draws the borough geometry above and differs only by the office it names

source.people: District Attorneys ship with the app from the city's own directory.

source.answers: Which U.S. House district covers this address, and who represents it.

boundary.label: Congressional districts from the Census Bureau's TIGERweb Legislative service, clipped to the city and shipped with the app

source.people: Members come from the unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset, refreshed weekly and reviewed before it ships.

source.answers: Which Civil (Municipal) Court district covers this address.

boundary.label: The 28 Civil Court districts from NYC Open Data (7vpq-4bh4), simplified and shipped with the app

source.people: No roster is joined; the card links the court rather than naming judges.

source.answers: Which New York State Senate district covers this address, and who holds the seat.

boundary.label: State Senate districts from the Census Bureau's TIGERweb Legislative service, clipped to the city and shipped with the app

source.people: Senators come from the NY Senate's Open Legislation API, refreshed weekly and reviewed before they ship; district offices are enriched from OpenStates where it publishes them.

source.answers: Which community school district this address is in.

boundary.label: Community school districts from NYC Open Data (8ugf-3d8u)

source.people: Superintendents are appointed rather than elected; the card links the district rather than naming one from an unverifiable list.

source.answers: Which Community Education Council serves this address.

boundary.label: The same community school district geometry from NYC Open Data (8ugf-3d8u) — a CEC serves one district

source.people: No roster ships. No CEC membership list is published in a form this app can verify, so the card links the council rather than naming people it cannot check.

source.answers: Which FDNY battalion covers this address.

boundary.label: FDNY battalion boundaries as the city publishes them to ArcGIS Online

source.people: No roster is joined; a battalion has no single officeholder to name.

guide.text: What Council district am I in?

source.answers: Which City Council district covers this address, and who represents it.

boundary.label: City Council districts from NYC Open Data (872g-cjhh)

source.people: Council Members are re-scraped weekly from council.nyc.gov's own district directory and reviewed before they ship.

guide.text: What community board am I in?

boundary.label: Community district boundaries from NYC Open Data (ruf7-3wgc), with board contact details from (5crt-au7u)

source.people: Board contact details come from the city's own community board dataset; individual members are not named.

layers.label: Election District
rank_comment: election-district (~4,200) sits just BEFORE its parent Assembly so the
Assembly outline frames its fills (same rule as police-sector below)

source.answers: Which election district this address votes in.

boundary.label: Election district boundaries as the city publishes them to ArcGIS Online

source.people: No roster: an election district has no officeholder.

source.answers: Which New York State Assembly district covers this address, and who holds the seat.

boundary.label: State Assembly districts from the Census Bureau's TIGERweb Legislative service, clipped to the city and shipped with the app

source.people: Assemblymembers come from the NY Senate's Open Legislation API, refreshed weekly and reviewed before they ship.

layers.label: NYPD Sector
layers.rank_note: 303 sectors — just before its parent precinct

source.answers: Which NYPD sector — the patrol area inside a precinct — covers this address.

boundary.label: Police sector boundaries from NYC Open Data (5rqd-h5ci)

source.people: No roster is joined; a sector has no separate commander to name.

source.answers: Which NYPD precinct covers this address, and who commands it.

boundary.label: Police precinct boundaries from NYC Open Data (y76i-bdw7)

source.people: Commanding officers are re-scraped weekly from the NYPD's own precinct pages. Where the NYPD publishes no commander the card says so rather than guessing — about four of the 78 at any time.

source.answers: Which Modified ZIP Code Tabulation Area contains this address.

boundary.label: MODZCTA boundaries from NYC Open Data (pri4-ifjk)

source.people: No roster: a ZIP code has no officeholder.

source.answers: Which Neighborhood Tabulation Area contains this address.

boundary.label: 2020 NTAs from NYC Open Data (9nt8-h7nd)

source.people: No roster: an NTA is a statistical area, and its name is not always the one a listing or a local would use.

source.answers: Which zoned high school serves this address, where one does.

boundary.label: High school zones from NYC Open Data (ruu9-egea)

source.people: No roster; most NYC high schools admit by application citywide rather than by zone, and the card says so where no zone applies.

source.answers: Which zoned middle school serves this address, where one does.

boundary.label: Middle school zones from NYC Open Data (t26j-jbq7)

source.people: No roster; the card links MySchools, which is what decides a placement.

source.answers: Which zoned elementary school serves this address.

boundary.label: Elementary school zones from NYC Open Data (cmjf-yawu)

source.people: No roster; the card links MySchools, which is what decides a placement.

source.answers: The nearest school sites to this point, by straight-line distance.

source.answers: The nearest police stations to this point, by straight-line distance.

source.answers: The nearest firehouses to this point, by straight-line distance.

source.answers: The nearest post offices to this point, by straight-line distance.

source.answers: The nearest public libraries to this point, by straight-line distance.

boundary.label: Library locations from NYC Open Data (feuq-due4)

source.people: No roster is joined. The dataset carries no phone number, which is a gap at the source rather than something the card withholds.

rosters.note: keys every precinct (even a null CO), so the floor is the precinct count, not the commander count

Known data gaps keyed by gap id, driving the Data gaps panel — emitted from the fleet guidebook's GUIDEBOOK:BEGIN gaps block by scripts/build_coverage_gaps.py, which reads this fork's this_metro key (--check is the drift gate). Network-first like the rosters: a closed gap should stop being advertised on the next visit.

honest placeholder (floor 0): CEC members are decentralized across 32 independent council sites with no scrapable central source or Open Data dataset; card links to the DOE hub (see scripts/cec_scraper.py)
10 offices (5 BP + 5 DA), operator-maintained from official sites; floor 5 = one entry per borough (build_borough_officials.py keys by borough)

data_sources.note: The machine-checked source manifest (Socrata ids, ArcGIS/TIGERweb endpoints, anchor provenance, year-search patterns) lives in the freshness gate ported in Phase 0.2, which already guards manifest<->app drift monthly. A second copy here would drift against it.
